judgements.title: Jira issue in title
judgements.question: Is this change substantial enough to warrant a Solr Jira issue under the contribution guidelines? A Jira issue is warranted only for a change that also warrants a changelog entry, i.e. one that Solr users or operators would notice. If it needs no release note (pure refactoring, test-only, build/CI, internal cleanup, typo fixes, documentation-only), answer no. Judge the change itself. This is advisory, not verification that an issue exists or that the referenced issue matches the change.

judgements.title: Changelog entry
judgements.question: Does this PR make a change that Solr users or operators would notice, and so warrants an entry in the release notes? Yes for: new features, bug fixes with user-visible symptoms, changed defaults or behavior, new/changed/removed parameters, APIs, config, metrics, CLI options, or performance changes users would notice. No for: pure refactoring, test-only changes, build/CI changes, internal cleanup, typo fixes, and documentation-only changes.

judgements.title: Reference Guide update
judgements.question: Does this PR add, change, or remove something documented (or that ought to be documented) in the Solr Reference Guide, such as a request parameter, a solrconfig.xml or schema setting, a system property or env var, a V1/V2 API, a CLI option, a metric, or a user-facing behavior, such that the Reference Guide (solr/solr-ref-guide) should be updated? Internal changes do not count.

judgements.title: Upgrade notes
judgements.question: Is this PR a backwards-incompatible change that users must act on when upgrading: a removed or renamed parameter, API, config element, class used by plugins, or a changed default that alters existing behavior? Answer no for additive changes and for changes to internal classes that plugins would not reasonably use.

judgements.title: Tests
judgements.question: Does this PR change non-trivial production logic (beyond refactoring, renames, logging, or comments) such that it should come with new or changed tests? Build, CI and developer tooling (workflows, Gradle build logic, scripts under dev-tools) does not need tests: answer no.
